reason: The premise that Ti-rich alloys can outperform Nb-Ta ones is supported by E1, and the baseline material's properties are confirmed by E2. However, the central mechanistic premise—that severe lattice distortion enhances electron–phonon coupling and raises Tc—is not directly supported by any cited evidence; E3 merely lists elemental Tc values, and E4 discusses phase separation with Sc, not Ti. The link between lattice distortion and Tc is therefore an unsupported extrapolation.
premises: Ti-rich Nb-Ti-based alloys exhibit better superconducting properties than Nb-Ta alloys
Severe lattice distortion from atomic size mismatch modifies the phonon spectrum and strengthens electron–phonon coupling
The baseline (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 is a single-phase bcc HEA with Tc ~7.7 K and robust superconductivity
Substituting Ti for Nb/Ta increases atomic size mismatch and local lattice distortion while maintaining a single-phase bcc structure
Increased lattice distortion raises Tc relative to Nb-Ta-dominated HEAs
